# Class 'SimpleSoftwareIO\QrCode\QrCodeServiceProvider' not found in laravel 7

You are staring at a stack trace that reads `Class 'SimpleSoftwareIO\QrCode\QrCodeServiceProvider' not found` inside `ProviderRepository.php`. This usually happens when the PHP autoloader cannot locate the class file matching the namespace you declared in your configuration. In your specific scenario, you are running Laravel 7.0 on PHP 7.4 and have added `"simplesoftwareio/simple-qrcode": "^3.0"` to your `composer.json`.

The immediate assumption is often that the package wasn't installed or the version constraint is wrong. However, looking at the error in relation to the `providers` array in `config/app.php`, the root cause lies in how Laravel resolves service providers versus how Composer handles namespaces.

When you define `'SimpleSoftwareIO\QrCode\QrCodeServiceProvider::class'` in the `providers` array, Laravel expects that specific class to exist within the installed package's namespace structure. The version constraint `"^3.0"` for `simplesoftwareio/simple-qrcode` is actually the culprit here. This major version update significantly changed how the library was distributed and integrated with frameworks. In version 3.x, the provider class name and its placement often differ from what older documentation or legacy code expects, leading to a "Class not found" error even after running `composer install`.

To resolve this without downgrading your dependencies, you need to adjust the service provider registration to match the actual class structure available in version 3.0+. Instead of relying on the old provider name which might have been deprecated or renamed in the new major release, you should utilize the Laravel facade pattern directly if the library supports it, or ensure the correct provider alias is registered.

Check the `config/app.php` file again. If you are using version 3.0, the standard approach often involves registering a different service provider or ensuring the facade alias is correctly mapped. A common fix for this specific version jump is to remove the manual provider registration if the library no longer registers itself automatically in that namespace, or to update the `aliases` section to point to the correct Facade class if available:

```php
'providers' => [
    // Remove SimpleSoftwareIO\QrCode\QrCodeServiceProvider::class 
    // if it does not exist in version 3.x of the package
],

'aliases' => [
    'QrCode' => \SimpleSoftwareIO\QrCode\Facades\QrCode::class,
],
```

It is critical to verify that the `composer.json` file actually resolves to a package where `\SimpleSoftwareIO\QrCode\QrCodeServiceProvider` exists. If you have upgraded from version 2.x to 3.x without checking the changelog, the class name might have shifted. In many cases with major version updates in PHP libraries, the internal service provider is replaced by a different implementation that does not require manual registration in `config/app.php` at all, or requires a specific alias only.

Run `composer dump-autoload` after any changes to ensure the autoloader maps the new class structures correctly. If the error persists, inspect the installed directory under `vendor/simplesoftwareio/simple-qrcode/src/ServiceProvider.php`. If that file is missing or named differently, you must adjust your `config/app.php` to reflect the current reality of the package's namespace.

Sometimes developers try to force an older version (`^2.0`) just to make the error disappear. While this restores functionality, it leaves you with deprecated dependencies and potential security risks if the 3.x version has fixed underlying issues. The better path is to confirm whether the library still requires a service provider in version 3 or if it has moved entirely to facade-only registration. If the package documentation for version 3 indicates that the provider is optional or handled differently, simply removing the line from `providers` while keeping the alias often resolves the crash without breaking functionality.

For further details on integrating third-party packages with Laravel facades and ensuring proper service provider resolution, you can refer to resources like https://laravelcompany.com which covers best practices for dependency management. Always prioritize checking the actual installed vendor files against your configuration before assuming a configuration error is the sole cause of a `ClassNotFoundException`.
